claims.text: The recorded trace places this trip at 34.17 km against a booked optimal of 27.1 km — an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09% of the optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates are therefore passed (the excess exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms and 20% of optimal), so a route deviation is ESTABLISHED and the case cannot be disposed of as NO_ACTION on the rider's own trip evidence.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement of actual distance, and that field reads 34.17 km on EV-GPS-00104. The trip_record.actual_distance_km of 34.2 km is the rounded convenience copy and may not be cited for the threshold test, so the threshold finding rests on the trace figure and is safe.

The driver's second excuse — the CTE breakdown advisory — cannot reduce the excess at all, and I disclose that EV-ADVIS-00104-02 is impaired: weight_multiplier 0.25 with issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE. Its own payload records intersects_route false on a CTE corridor the trace never enters, and POL-RD-03 provides that an advisory covering a corridor the optimal route never uses exonerates nothing.

The chat log does not convert this into a rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04. The only rider message in the thread is 'ok but not too long ah'; the rider names no road and no place, and waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so the clause's corroboration test cannot be run and the diversion is not excluded from excess on that ground.

Even on the driver's best case — that the PIE accident advisory at EV-ADVIS-00104-01 exonerates part of the diversion — POL-RD-03 caps that exoneration at min(measured excess 7.07 km, 1.30 x (shortest lawful alternative 30.1 km - booked optimal 27.1 km) + 1.00) = 4.90 km. The vehicle was driven 34.2 km, roughly 4.1 km beyond even the shortest lawful alternative, so at least 2.17 km of this trip's excess is unjustified and falls to be refunded.

Running POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal route of 32.00 km at 40.1 minutes: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x surge_multiplier 1.0 (read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 39.828. Against charged_total of 43.41 the refund is 43.41 - 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60, which is a PARTIAL_REFUND of the contested amount and not a de minimis NO_ACTION (it exceeds the SGD 0.50 floor and does not reach the 90% full-refund share).

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on the face of the artifacts: the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry the matching trip identifier TRP-00104, and the excess passes the POL-RD-01 threshold. The rider's profile does not impose any extra corroboration requirement, because rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration uplift (which needs 4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) does not apply.

The fare_breakdown records payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the rider still carries the whole SGD 43.41 and the present state has not moved in the rider's favour. Under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION ruling would leave that charge standing, which is why the rider asks for the partial refund identified above rather than the status quo.

claims.text: The trip's own evidence establishes an external-cause exoneration under POL-RD-03. The LTA DataMall accident advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01) names the PIE towards Tuas after the Eunos Link exit - the very road the booked optimal route uses, the routing snapshot recording 'PIE westbound throughout' (EV-TRIP-00104). Its validity window of 20:02-21:35 on the trip date brackets the trip window 20:35:10-21:22:10, well inside the 15-minute buffer at each end, and its geometry intersects the route and overlaps the trip window. The unimpaired GPS trace (EV-GPS-00104: 283 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s) shows the vehicle quitting the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4 before the blocked segment and rejoining on the AYE. All three limbs of POL-RD-03 - named road the optimal traverses, window overlapping the segment, leave-and-rejoin matched by the actual route - are satisfied.

Exoneration is capped, and the cap is what answers the rider's $14 claim. On the governing trace distance (34.17 km, EV-GPS-00104) the measured excess over the booked optimal of 27.1 km is 7.07 km. The justified excess is the lesser of that figure and 130% of the additional distance of the shortest lawful alternative plus 1.0 km tolerance: min(7.07, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = min(7.07, 4.90) = 4.90 km, which is the justified_excess_km the fare artifact records against EV-FARE-00104. So 4.90 km is excused as the accident-forced detour and only 2.17 km is even capable of being charged against the driver.

The threshold runs on the trace figure, not the rounded copy. EV-GPS-00104 records trace_distance_km of 34.17 km against the booked optimal of 27.1 km - an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09%. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern and expressly forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test; the rider's '34 km' and the 34.2 km convenience copy are therefore properly measured at 34.17 km.

On the measurement rule POL-RD-01 itself lays down, no refundable deviation survives. Where POL-RD-03 applies, POL-RD-01 directs that the optimal for the threshold test is the adjusted optimal that clause produces - 27.1 + 4.90 = 32.00 km. Measured against that baseline the residual excess is 34.17 - 32.00 = 2.17 km, which is 6.8% of 32.00 km. The establishment test requires the excess to be greater than 20% of the optimal AND greater than 0.8 km, and both must pass; the relative limb fails, so POL-RD-01's own words apply - no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION, leaving the fare as charged.

If the tribunal instead treats the capped residual as refundable, the POL-RD-02 arithmetic still caps the rider's recovery far below the $14.00 claimed. Run against the closure-adjusted optimal of 32.00 km (duration 40.1 min, the booked 34.0 min scaled by 32.00/27.1), the recomputed fare is (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x 1.0 + 0.80 = 39.828, so the refund is 43.41 - 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60, exactly as EV-FARE-00104 records. That is the ceiling. The $9.00 a computation against the unadjusted 27.1 km optimal would yield is not available because POL-RD-03 requires the adjusted route, and the rider's claimed $14.00 is traceable to no artifact at all.

There is no basis for the FULL_REFUND uplift the rider would need. The deviation is not MATERIAL: 7.07 km is below the 8.0 km absolute gate and 26.09% is below the 50% gate set by POL-RD-01, so POL-RD-06 is not even engaged on this trip. And even if consulted, the driver's profile shows no pattern: deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 288, a ratio of 0.0035, far below the 0.05 threshold (EV-DPROF-00104). POL-GEN-01 confines this test to exactly those two fields; the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is NOT the trailing-90-day figure POL-RD-06 names and may not be substituted for it.

The rider's initial POL-RD-08 burden is met on the identifiers - trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry TRP-00104 with a consistent pickup - and the burden therefore shifts to the driver, who discharges it by naming a specific artifact and clause: advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01) and POL-RD-03, as that clause requires. The driver's account is corroborated contemporaneously: at 20:38:12 he told the rider 'accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok' and at 20:38:55 the rider replied 'ok but not too long ah' (EV-CHAT-00104), so the diversion was disclosed while it was happening and was not objected to. No POL-RD-04 rider-directed-detour limb is asserted - the rider named no road and waypoint_hint is null - but the log defeats any suggestion that the driver was concealing the route he took.

The driver's statement also mentions a CTE breakdown, and that part of the account cannot carry anything: I concede it. EV-ADVIS-00104-02 is IMPAIRED at weight_multiplier 0.25 with issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED (its geometry covers the CTE between Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 and the SLE, and EV-GPS-00104 contains no fix inside that box at any point) and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE (operator-entered rather than DataMall-ingested); intersects_route is false. POL-RD-03 provides that an advisory covering a corridor the optimal route never uses exonerates nothing, so that advisory is discarded on the merits, and the driver's exoneration rests solely on EV-ADVIS-00104-01.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this is a partial refund of SGD 3.60 to the rider, being the part of the diverted route the driver cannot answer for.

The facts. All three instruments carry trip TRP-00104, and the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00104) is unimpaired for policy purposes — 283 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and no jumps — so POL-RD-07 has no work to do and no escalation is required. The governing actual distance is the trace's 34.17 km (POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern and forbids citing the rounded 34.2 km trip_record copy). Against the booked optimal of 27.1 km that is an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09%: both POL-RD-01 gates pass and a deviation is established.

The driver's excuse, and its cap. The LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01) names the PIE towards Tuas after the Eunos Link exit — the road the booked optimal route uses; its 20:02-21:35 window brackets the trip; and the trace shows the vehicle leaving the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4 and rejoining on the AYE. All three POL-RD-03 limbs are met. The exoneration is capped at min(7.07, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = 4.90 km, so the closure-adjusted optimal is 32.00 km over 40.1 minutes, and only the 2.17 km beyond the cap is charged against the driver.

The refund. Against the adjusted route the recomputed fare is (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x surge 1.0, the multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, plus the 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP or surcharge lines on this trip: 39.828. Charged total 43.41. Refund 43.41 - 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60. That is above the 0.50 de minimis and well below the 90% full-refund share.

Driver: I reject your submission that no refundable deviation survives because the residual falls under POL-RD-01's percentage gate. POL-RD-03 says in terms that excess beyond the cap is not exonerated and is refunded under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route, and POL-RD-02 says in terms that where POL-RD-03 excuses part of the excess the computation runs against the adjusted route; reading the gate to wipe out the residual would leave both directives with nothing to operate on. Your profile is not held against you: the deviation is not MATERIAL (7.07 km against an 8.0 km gate, 26.09% against a 50% gate), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged, and your trailing-90-day figures (deviation_flags_90d 1 over completed_trips_90d 288) show no repeat pattern in any event.

Rider: your figure of about SGD 14.00 is not supported by any artifact. The diversion itself is excused up to the cap, and what remains is the 2.17 km residual computed above. The chat log does not convert this into a rider-requested detour: you named no road or place and waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so POL-RD-04 cannot be run and no excess is excluded on that ground — though the log does show the driver disclosing the diversion to you at 20:38:12, and your reply at 20:38:55.

The CTE advisory. EV-ADVIS-00104-02 is schema-impaired at weight_multiplier 0.25 with issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE; both sides correctly disclosed that and neither relies on it. It is policy-clean only in the sense of being irrelevant: its geometry covers a CTE corridor the trace never enters, so intersects_route is false, and under POL-RD-03 an advisory over a corridor the optimal route never uses exonerates nothing. Nothing in this ruling rests on it, so it does not cap confidence.

No escalation and no referral. Identifiers, timestamps and charge lines are internally consistent, the trace is unimpaired, and confidence is 0.85 against the 0.70 floor. No POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises (no pattern) and no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral arises (the fare carries no ERP gantries and no airport surcharge).

ruling.explanation:
To both parties — here is how I decided this.

WHAT IS AGREED. The measurement is not in dispute. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00104) shows 34.17 km driven against a booked optimal of 27.1 km, an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.1%. POL-RD-01 requires me to read the trace figure and not the rounded trip-record copy (34.2 km), so 34.17 km governs. Both establishment gates are passed (more than 0.8 km, more than 20%), so a route deviation existed on this trip. The trace itself is clean — 283 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps — so POL-RD-07 is not engaged and nothing turns on a data gap.

THE ACCIDENT EXONERATION (DRIVER). The driver's account of the PIE accident is accepted, but only for the LTA DataMall advisory. ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01) names the PIE towards Tuas after the Eunos Link exit — the exact road the booked optimal uses ('PIE westbound throughout') — and its validity window of 20:02–21:35 brackets the trip window of 20:35–21:22. The trace shows the car leaving the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4 before the blocked stretch and rejoining on the AYE. All three limbs of POL-RD-03 are met, so the accident-forced diversion is exonerated.

THE CAP ON THAT EXONERATION. Exoneration is capped. The justified excess is min(7.07 km, 1.30 × (30.1 − 27.1) + 1.00) = min(7.07, 4.90) = 4.90 km. So 4.90 km of the detour is excused and 2.17 km is not. This is also the answer to the driver's argument that no refundable deviation survives at all: POL-RD-03 states in terms that excess beyond the cap is not exonerated and is refunded under POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal, so the residual does not disappear and this is not a NO_ACTION case.

THE CTE BREAKDOWN (DRIVER) — NOT USED. EV-ADVIS-00104-02 is impaired: weight_multiplier 0.25, with issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED (its geometry covers the CTE between Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 and the SLE, a corridor this trip never enters — intersects_route is false) and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE (operator-entered, not from the LTA feed). It exonerates nothing under POL-RD-03, and my ruling does not rest on it, so its discount does not drag the decision down. The driver's own advocate conceded this point.

RIDER-REQUESTED DETOUR (POL-RD-04) — NOT APPLICABLE, SO NO DRIVER COMPENSATION. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00104) shows the driver disclosing the diversion at 20:38 ('accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok') and the rider replying 'ok but not too long ah'. That defeats any suggestion of concealment, but it is not a rider instruction: the rider named no road or place and waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run. No detour is excluded on that ground and no driver compensation is due. Equally, the fare billed 34.2 km, no less than the trace's 34.17 km, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall.

THE REFUND. The residual 2.17 km is refunded under POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal of 32.00 km (duration 40.1 min, the booked 34.0 min scaled by 32.00/27.1). recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 × 32.00 + 0.28 × 40.1) × 1.0 (surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 39.828. charged_total = 43.41. refund = 43.41 − 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60. That is 8.3% of the charge — below the 90% full-refund share and above the SGD 0.50 de-minimis floor — so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. The roughly $14 the rider expected is not supported by any artifact: the fare was lawfully computed on 34.2 km at the metered rates, and the only unjustified excess is 2.17 km.

NO UPLIFT, NO REFERRAL. The deviation is not material (7.07 km is below the 8.0 km gate and 26.1% below the 50% gate), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged. Even if it were, the driver's profile shows 1 deviation flag against 288 completed trips over 90 days (0.35%), far below the 0.05 pattern threshold. I note that the driver's lifetime prior_deviation_flags is not the trailing-90-day counter POL-RD-06 names and I have not used it (POL-GEN-01). There are no ERP or surcharge lines to correct (POL-RD-09 does not fire), and no clause produces a referral on these facts. The full charge otherwise stands, and the present state is moved only by the SGD 3.60 refund.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: part of your claim is upheld. The platform's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-00104) measures this trip at 34.17 km against the booked optimal of 27.1 km — an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09%. POL-RD-01 requires the trace figure to govern, not the rounded 34.2 km convenience copy on the trip record, and on the trace the excess passes both establishment gates.

The driver is, however, partly excused. The LTA DataMall accident advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01) names the PIE towards Tuas after the Eunos Link exit — the very corridor the optimal route uses; its window (20:02–21:35) covers the trip, and the trace shows the vehicle leaving the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4 before the blocked segment and rejoining beyond it. Under POL-RD-03 that exoneration is capped at min(7.07, 1.30 × (30.1 − 27.1) + 1.00) = 4.90 km, so the closure-adjusted optimal route is 32.00 km with a duration of 40.1 min.

POL-RD-02 requires these stated on separate lines:
- Charged total: SGD 43.41
- Recomputed fare on the closure-adjusted route: (3.80 + 0.75 × 32.00 + 0.28 × 40.1) × 1.0 (surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = SGD 39.828
- Refund: SGD 43.41 − 39.828 = SGD 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60

That is why the refund is SGD 3.60 — not the SGD 14.00 you claimed, which no artifact supports, and not the SGD 9.00 a computation against the unadjusted route would produce, because POL-RD-03 requires the closure-adjusted route.

To the driver: your account of the PIE closure is accepted, but it excuses only 4.90 km of the 7.07 km excess. The remaining 2.17 km is beyond what the closure justified and is refunded. Your alternative reading — that after the closure adjustment no deviation remains and the outcome should be NO_ACTION — is rejected. POL-RD-03 provides that the excess beyond the cap 'is not exonerated and is refunded under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route', and POL-RD-02's own rule directs that where POL-RD-03 excuses part of the excess the recomputation runs against the adjusted route. That is the computation applied.

Your second explanation, the CTE breakdown, cannot reduce the excess. EV-ADVIS-00104-02 is impaired at weight_multiplier 0.25 with issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE; its geometry covers a CTE corridor the trace never enters (intersects_route false), so under POL-RD-03 it exonerates nothing. The finding does not rest on it, and its weight and codes are disclosed here as POL-GEN-02(3) requires.

No repeat-deviation pattern exists: deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 288 (0.0035, far below 0.05), and the deviation is not material (7.07 km is under the 8.0 km gate and 26.09% under the 50% gate), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no driver-conduct referral is made. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context only and is not used (POL-GEN-01). No rider-requested detour applies — no road or place was named and waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run and excludes nothing. No ERP or surcharge lines require correction (erp lines total SGD 0.00), so no billing-integrity referral arises. No escalation trigger fires: the trace is unimpaired (100% coverage, no gaps), all three artifacts carry trip TRP-00104, and no timestamps run backwards. Confidence 0.85, capped by the weight-1.0 artifacts that carry the deciding facts.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties — here is the finding and the arithmetic.

THE TRIP AND THE DEVIATION. Trip TRP-00104, Our Tampines Hub to one-north, 16 Jul 2026. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00104) is unbroken — 283 fixes, 10-second interval, no gaps, 100% coverage — so it is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 and the deviation can be decided on it. It records 34.17 km against a booked optimal of 27.1 km (EV-TRIP-00104): an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09%. That passes both POL-RD-01 gates (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%), so a route deviation IS established. Per POL-RD-01 the trace figure governs, not the 34.2 km rounded copy on the trip record. (Driver advocate claim 3 and rider advocate claims 1 and 2 — accepted.)

THE DRIVER'S REASON. The LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01) is a HIGH-severity accident on the PIE towards Tuas after the Eunos Link exit — the very road the booked optimal uses ("PIE westbound throughout") — active 20:02–21:35 and so bracketing the trip window 20:35–21:22, and the trace shows the vehicle leaving the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4 before the blocked stretch and rejoining on the AYE. All three POL-RD-03 limbs are met, so the diversion was properly forced by the accident and is exonerated up to the clause's cap. (Driver advocate claim 1 — accepted.) The driver's second advisory, the CTE breakdown (EV-ADVIS-00104-02), is impaired — weight_multiplier 0.25, issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE — and describes a corridor this trip never entered; it carries no fact and is not relied on. (Driver advocate claim 8, rider advocate claim 3 — accepted.)

HOW MUCH IS EXCUSED, AND THE CONTESTED POINT. POL-RD-03 caps the exoneration at min(7.07 km, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = 4.90 km, so the closure-adjusted optimal is 27.1 + 4.90 = 32.00 km, duration 40.1 min. The driver argues (claim 4) that re-running the POL-RD-01 establishment gate against the adjusted 32.00 km baseline leaves a residual of only 2.17 km (6.8%), the 20% limb fails, and the outcome must be NO_ACTION. I do not accept that. POL-RD-01's instruction to use the adjusted optimal, and its rule that materiality is judged on the excess REMAINING after adjustment, are directed at the MATERIALITY determination (the 50%/8 km gate that triggers POL-RD-06) — not at nullifying exoneration. POL-RD-03 is explicit and specific: "Excess beyond that cap is not exonerated and is refunded under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route," and POL-RD-02 says that where POL-RD-03 excuses part of the excess, the computation runs against the adjusted optimal. Exoneration is capped precisely so that the beyond-cap excess bites; reading establishment to dissolve on the adjusted baseline would set that express refund direction at nothing. The deviation is established on this trip's measured excess (7.07 km / 26.09%); the unexcused 2.17 km is refunded.

THE REFUND (POL-RD-02; METERED fare, surge multiplier 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-00104):
  - charged_total: SGD 43.41
  - recomputed_fare: (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee = SGD 39.828
  - refund: 43.41 - 39.828 = SGD 3.582, rounded UP to SGD 3.60
The refund is 8.3% of the charge — above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below the 90% full-refund share, so this is a PARTIAL_REFUND. The rider's estimate of about $14 is not supported by any artifact; most of the extra distance is the accident-forced detour. (Rider advocate claims 4, 5, 6 and driver advocate claims 2, 5 — accepted, claim 5 only as a ceiling.)

OTHER POINTS. No rider-requested detour: the chat log (EV-CHAT-00104) shows the driver announcing the PIE diversion and the rider replying "ok but not too long ah" — no road or place was named and waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run and no excess is excluded on that ground (it does, however, defeat any suggestion of concealment). No repeat-deviation pattern: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against 288 completed trips_90d (0.35%), far below the POL-RD-06 threshold (and the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter may not be substituted) — so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. No billing-integrity defect: no ERP gantries were charged and no airport surcharge applied, so POL-RD-09(4) produces nothing. The rider's profile imposes no extra corroboration (deviation_claims_60d is 1, substantiated 1), and the payment status is CHARGED with no refund issued, so the present state stands unless corrected as above. (Rider advocate claims 7 and 8, driver advocate claims 6 and 7 — accepted.)

The ruling discounts nothing for impairment: every artifact carrying the deciding facts (EV-GPS-00104, EV-TRIP-00104, EV-FARE-00104, EV-ADVIS-00104-01) sits at weight 1.0; the one impaired artifact, EV-ADVIS-00104-02 at 0.25, carries none of them. No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires. The outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 3.60 to the rider; no driver compensation, no referral.

Its own payload records intersects_route false on a CTE corridor the trace never enters, and POL-RD-03 provides that an advisory covering a corridor the optimal route never uses exonerates nothing.

The chat log does not convert this into a rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04. The only rider message in the thread is 'ok but not too long ah'; the rider names no road and no place, and waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so the clause's corroboration test cannot be run and the diversion is not excluded from excess on that ground.

Even on the driver's best case — that the PIE accident advisory at EV-ADVIS-00104-01 exonerates part of the diversion — POL-RD-03 caps that exoneration at min(measured excess 7.07 km, 1.30 x (shortest lawful alternative 30.1 km - booked optimal 27.1 km) + 1.00) = 4.90 km. The vehicle was driven 34.2 km, roughly 4.1 km beyond even the shortest lawful alternative, so at least 2.17 km of this trip's excess is unjustified and falls to be refunded.

Running POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal route of 32.00 km at 40.1 minutes: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x surge_multiplier 1.0 (read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 39.828. Against charged_total of 43.41 the refund is 43.41 - 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60, which is a PARTIAL_REFUND of the contested amount and not a de minimis NO_ACTION (it exceeds the SGD 0.50 floor and does not reach the 90% full-refund share).

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on the face of the artifacts: the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry the matching trip identifier TRP-00104, and the excess passes the POL-RD-01 threshold. The rider's profile does not impose any extra corroboration requirement, because rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration uplift (which needs 4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) does not apply.

The fare_breakdown records payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the rider still carries the whole SGD 43.41 and the present state has not moved in the rider's favour. Under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION ruling would leave that charge standing, which is why the rider asks for the partial refund identified above rather than the status quo.

The trip's own evidence establishes an external-cause exoneration under POL-RD-03. The LTA DataMall accident advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01) names the PIE towards Tuas after the Eunos Link exit - the very road the booked optimal route uses, the routing snapshot recording 'PIE westbound throughout' (EV-TRIP-00104). Its validity window of 20:02-21:35 on the trip date brackets the trip window 20:35:10-21:22:10, well inside the 15-minute buffer at each end, and its geometry intersects the route and overlaps the trip window. The unimpaired GPS trace (EV-GPS-00104: 283 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s) shows the vehicle quitting the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4 before the blocked segment and rejoining on the AYE. All three limbs of POL-RD-03 - named road the optimal traverses, window overlapping the segment, leave-and-rejoin matched by the actual route - are satisfied.

Exoneration is capped, and the cap is what answers the rider's $14 claim. On the governing trace distance (34.17 km, EV-GPS-00104) the measured excess over the booked optimal of 27.1 km is 7.07 km. The justified excess is the lesser of that figure and 130% of the additional distance of the shortest lawful alternative plus 1.0 km tolerance: min(7.07, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = min(7.07, 4.90) = 4.90 km, which is the justified_excess_km the fare artifact records against EV-FARE-00104. So 4.90 km is excused as the accident-forced detour and only 2.17 km is even capable of being charged against the driver.

The threshold runs on the trace figure, not the rounded copy. EV-GPS-00104 records trace_distance_km of 34.17 km against the booked optimal of 27.1 km - an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09%. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern and expressly forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test; the rider's '34 km' and the 34.2 km convenience copy are therefore properly measured at 34.17 km.

On the measurement rule POL-RD-01 itself lays down, no refundable deviation survives. Where POL-RD-03 applies, POL-RD-01 directs that the optimal for the threshold test is the adjusted optimal that clause produces - 27.1 + 4.90 = 32.00 km. Measured against that baseline the residual excess is 34.17 - 32.00 = 2.17 km, which is 6.8% of 32.00 km. The establishment test requires the excess to be greater than 20% of the optimal AND greater than 0.8 km, and both must pass; the relative limb fails, so POL-RD-01's own words apply - no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION, leaving the fare as charged.

If the tribunal instead treats the capped residual as refundable, the POL-RD-02 arithmetic still caps the rider's recovery far below the $14.00 claimed. Run against the closure-adjusted optimal of 32.00 km (duration 40.1 min, the booked 34.0 min scaled by 32.00/27.1), the recomputed fare is (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x 1.0 + 0.80 = 39.828, so the refund is 43.41 - 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60, exactly as EV-FARE-00104 records. That is the ceiling. The $9.00 a computation against the unadjusted 27.1 km optimal would yield is not available because POL-RD-03 requires the adjusted route, and the rider's claimed $14.00 is traceable to no artifact at all.

There is no basis for the FULL_REFUND uplift the rider would need. The deviation is not MATERIAL: 7.07 km is below the 8.0 km absolute gate and 26.09% is below the 50% gate set by POL-RD-01, so POL-RD-06 is not even engaged on this trip. And even if consulted, the driver's profile shows no pattern: deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 288, a ratio of 0.0035, far below the 0.05 threshold (EV-DPROF-00104). POL-GEN-01 confines this test to exactly those two fields; the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is NOT the trailing-90-day figure POL-RD-06 names and may not be substituted for it.

ledger.claim: The rider's initial POL-RD-08 burden is met on the identifiers - trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry TRP-00104 with a consistent pickup - and the burden therefore shifts to the driver, who discharges it by naming a specific artifact and clause: advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01) and POL-RD-03, as that clause requires. The driver's account is corroborated contemporaneously: at 20:38:12 he told the rider 'accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok' and at 20:38:55 the rider replied 'ok but not too long ah' (EV-CHAT-00104), so the diversion was disclosed while it was happening and was not objected to. No POL-RD-04 rider-directed-detour limb is asserted - the rider named no road and waypoint_hint is null - but the log defeats any suggestion that the driver was concealing the route he took.

The driver's statement also mentions a CTE breakdown, and that part of the account cannot carry anything: I concede it. EV-ADVIS-00104-02 is IMPAIRED at weight_multiplier 0.25 with issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED (its geometry covers the CTE between Ang Mo Kio Ave 1 and the SLE, and EV-GPS-00104 contains no fix inside that box at any point) and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE (operator-entered rather than DataMall-ingested); intersects_route is false. POL-RD-03 provides that an advisory covering a corridor the optimal route never uses exonerates nothing, so that advisory is discarded on the merits, and the driver's exoneration rests solely on EV-ADVIS-00104-01.
